claims: The Artemis II mission costs over $4 billion per launch.
The NASA Artemis program is projected to exceed $90–$100 billion in total expenditures by 2025–2026.
The Artemis II mission's per launch cost is estimated at over $4 billion ($4.1–$4.2 billion) per mission for SLS and Orion.
The NASA Artemis program's total costs are projected at $93 billion to $105 billion through 2025–2028.
The NASA Artemis program's total costs cover development, infrastructure, and operations.
The costs cover the development and operation of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule for the four-person crewed lunar flyby.
Lockheed Martin built the Orion capsule.
The Boeing-built SLS rocket and Lockheed Martin-built Orion capsule have faced significant cost overruns.
The Apollo program cost an estimated $290 billion in today’s money to achieve the first landing.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled for 2026.
The Artemis II mission involves a 10-day crewed journey around the Moon.
